results.content:
# Last passengers leave virus-hit cruise ship as three more test positive

The last passengers have left the hantavirus-hit cruise ship, as authorities confirmed three new positive cases linked to the deadly outbreak.

The MV Hondius departed Tenerife for the Netherlands on Monday after its final six passengers - four Australians, one Briton and one New Zealander - and some crew members disembarked.

Three passengers have died after travelling on the ship, two of whom were confirmed to have had the virus.

An American and a French national who had previously returned home have tested positive, authorities said. Nine cases of hantavirus linked to the MV Hondius have been confirmed, with two others suspected, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). [...] An elderly Dutch man was the first passenger who died on board the MV Hondius on 11 April. He had earlier developed symptoms and is believed to have been the first infected in the outbreak, but died before he could be tested.

His wife left the ship on 24 April on the island of St Helena and flew to South Africa. She died two days later in a clinic in Johannesburg.

A German woman died on board the cruise ship on 2 May. Both women are confirmed cases.

The MV Hondius had been carrying 147 passengers and crew from 23 countries after departing from Ushuaia in Argentina on 1 April.

Title: Swiss Hantavirus Case Linked to MV Hondius Outbreak
Latest News in One Second. # Swiss Hantavirus Case Linked to MV Hondius Outbreak. Three suspected hantavirus case patients are evacuated from the MV Hondius cruise ship on Wednesday.@drtedros via X. Swiss health officials confirmed a new hantavirus case in Zurich on Wednesday, May 6, 2026, involving a traveler from the MV Hondius cruise ship. The discovery coincides with the medical evacuation of three suspected patients from the vessel currently anchored off the coast of Cape Verde. The World Health Organization (WHO) identified the pathogen as the Andes strain, which is capable of person-to-person transmission. While three passengers have died during the voyage, laboratory testing has confirmed three of the eight total suspected cases to date, according to the WHO. The patient in Switzerland sought medical attention after receiving an electronic notification from the cruise operator. The Swiss government stated that the individual is receiving treatment and emphasized that the broader population faces no immediate threat. Addressing the nature of the virus, WHO epidemiologist Maria Van Kerkhove explained that transmission requires very specific conditions rather than casual contact. "Hantavirus, unlike influenza or Covid-19, is only transmissible from person to person through close contact, such as sharing a bed or food," said Maria Van Kerkhove, WHO epidemiologist. Regarding the evacuation on Wednesday morning, cruise operator Oceanwide Expeditions confirmed that the transfer involved individuals showing significant signs of illness. "two of them had "acute symptoms,"" said Oceanwide Expeditions, Cruise operator. The Dutch foreign ministry detailed the logistics of the medical transfer, noting that the patients were moved to specialized European facilities. The MV Hondius remains in a standoff near West Africa after local authorities denied docking rights. While the Spanish national government offered a port in the Canary Islands, regional leader Fernando Clavijo voiced strong opposition to the plan. "This decision is not based on any technical criteria, nor is there sufficient information to reassure the public or guarantee their safety," said Fernando Clavijo, regional leader. results.content:
Three confirmed deaths have been linked to the outbreak.

The first victim was a 70-year-old Dutch man who fell ill en route to Saint Helena, presenting with fever, headache, abdominal pain, and diarrhea.

He died on 11 April 2026 aboard the ship; his body was later removed at the British territory of Saint Helena for eventual repatriation.

His 69-year-old wife, also Dutch, continued onward.

She collapsed at OR Tambo International Airport in Johannesburg, South Africa, while attempting to connect to a flight home to the Netherlands.

She was rushed to a nearby health facility in the Kempton Park area but died shortly after arrival.

A third passenger, a German national, died on 2 May 2026 while still aboard the ship; his body remains on the vessel.

(Source: news24.com) [...] (Source: news24.com)

Laboratory testing has confirmed hantavirus in at least two cases: the Dutch woman who died after collapsing at OR Tambo and the British passenger now hospitalised.

The husband’s and the German passenger’s deaths are suspected but not yet fully confirmed as hantavirus via lab results.

South Africa’s Department of Health and the World Health Organization (WHO) are treating the cluster as a suspected hantavirus outbreak.

(Source: bbc.com)

A 69-year-old British national is in intensive care at a private hospital in Sandton, Johannesburg, South Africa.

He became seriously ill near Ascension Island after the ship left Saint Helena and was medically evacuated to South Africa on 27 April 2026.

His condition is described as critical but stable. [...] The incident, unfolding over weeks in the remote South Atlantic, highlights the challenges of managing infectious diseases on vessels far from major medical facilities.

The dire situation has sparked international concern.

(Source: apnews.com)

The MV Hondius departed Ushuaia, Argentina, around 1 April 2026, carrying 88 passengers and 61 crew from 23 nationalities, including 17 Americans and 23 Britons, on a polar expedition that included Antarctica, the Falkland Islands, and a transatlantic crossing toward Spain’s Canary Islands.

Symptoms first appeared during the voyage, initially mistaken for severe acute respiratory infections.

(Source: yahoo.com)

Three confirmed deaths have been linked to the outbreak.
